title: Generics, impl Trait, and dyn
summary: Three ways to say "some type with this capability" — compile-time, anonymous, or runtime.
lecture: `fn largest<T: PartialOrd>(list: &[T])` is monomorphized: the compiler stamps out a concrete copy per type used — zero runtime cost, and the bound (`PartialOrd` because the body uses `>`) is the whole requirement.
`-> impl Iterator<Item = i32>` returns a real concrete type without naming it — essential for iterator chains and closures whose types are unwritable. Still fully static.

`Box<dyn Draw>` defers to runtime: a fat pointer with a vtable, letting one Vec hold circles AND squares. The cost is a heap allocation and dynamic dispatch; the payoff is heterogeneity. A bare `dyn Draw` can't stand alone — it's unsized, so it lives behind Box, &, or Rc.
Default to generics; reach for dyn when you genuinely need mixed types in one collection or API.

example.caption: Static when you can, dynamic when you must.
